title: Ensure CockroachDB Cluster is Initialized Securely with TLS
description: CockroachDB clusters must be initialized and operated in secure mode so that all inter- node and client-node communication uses TLS with certificates signed by a trusted CA. CockroachDB's production documentation strongly recommends running secure clusters (with --certs-dir and valid certificates) instead of using --insecure, which disables all encryption and authentication.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.3 Ensure CockroachDB Cluster is Initialized Securely with TLS

audit.command: Run ps -ef | grep "[c]ockroach start": --insecure must not appear (--accept-sql-without-tls is also a weakness). Verify the certs directory (e.g. /var/lib/cockroach/certs) contains ca.crt, node.crt/node.key and client certificates, is owned by cockroach, and that the CA key is kept off the nodes. Confirm cockroach sql --insecure is rejected.

remediation.command: 1. Generate the cluster Certificate Authority (CA): The documentation suggests creating two directories on your local machine: certs (for public files) and my-safe-directory (for the private CA key). On a secure workstation: # Create directories for certificates # `certs` : You'll generate your CA certificate and all node and client certificates and keys in this directory.

title: Do Not Use the --insecure Flag in Production Environments Under Any Circumstances
description: CockroachDB supports an --insecure startup option that disables all node-to-node and client-to-node encryption, authentication, and certificate validation. When started in this mode, the cluster operates entirely without Transport Layer Security (TLS), allowing unauthenticated and unencrypted connections. This option exists only for initial testing or ephemeral local development. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when no running cockroach start process uses --insecure (FAIL when no node process is running). Also grep the node log for "RUNNING IN INSECURE MODE".
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.4 Do Not Use the --insecure Flag in Production Environments Under Any Circumstances

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo args= | grep '[c]ockroach start') || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -c -- '--insecure' || true

remediation.command: Stop the insecure nodes, create a CA and node/client certificates (cockroach cert create-ca / create-node / create-client), replace --insecure with --certs-dir=<certs> in the systemd unit and restart the nodes.

title: Secure the root User and Administrative Roles
description: The root user in CockroachDB has unrestricted administrative privileges across the entire cluster. Because compromise of root grants full control, its use must be tightly restricted and secured. The root account should authenticate exclusively with TLS client certificates (mTLS), and password authentication must be disabled.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.3 Secure the root User and Administrative Roles

audit.command: Run SHOW CLUSTER SETTING server.host_based_authentication.configuration; rules for root must use cert (cert-*) methods only and be limited to jump-host CIDRs, followed by host all root all reject. Run SHOW ROLES and SHOW GRANTS ON ROLE admin: membership of admin must be limited to approved administrators, and applications must not connect as root.

remediation.command: 1. Enforce certificate-only authentication for root Update the HBA configuration to allow only certificate-based methods: SET CLUSTER SETTING server.host_based_authentication.configuration = ' TYPE DATABASE USER ADDRESS METHOD host all root <jumpbox-cidr> cert host all root all reject '; Replace <jumpbox-cidr> with your actual admin network. 2. Restrict root usage operationally - Replace script usage with least-privilege service accounts.

title: Ensure Encryption at Rest Keys Are Managed by an External KMS and Retrieved at Startup
description: CockroachDB supports the use of external key management systems (KMS), such as HashiCorp Vault, to securely manage and deliver encryption keys used for encryption at rest. External key managers provide a centralized and auditable way to store and rotate keys and supply them dynamically to CockroachDB at startup.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.7 Ensure Encryption at Rest Keys Are Managed by an External KMS and Retrieved at Startup

audit.command: Run ps -ef | grep -- "--enterprise-encryption": every encrypted store must have --enterprise-encryption=path=...,key=...,old-key=...,rotation-period=... Check the systemd unit and wrapper scripts (grep -Ri vault /etc/cockroach /etc/systemd/system) to confirm the store key is fetched from an external KMS (e.g. Vault) at startup rather than kept on the data volume.

remediation.command: 1. Deploy or connect to a supported key management system: Such as HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS, or another trusted external provider. 2. Configure the Systemd Service to enable encryption: Edit the service file at /etc/systemd/system/cockroach.service.

title: Ensure Network Time Protocol (NTP) Service Is Configured for Cluster Clock Synchronization
description: CockroachDB requires moderate levels of clock synchronization to preserve data consistency. When a node detects that its clock is out of sync with at least half of the other nodes in the cluster by 80% of the maximum offset allowed (500 ms by default), it will spontaneously shut down to avoid consistency anomalies.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.1 Ensure Network Time Protocol (NTP) Service Is Configured for Cluster Clock Synchronization

audit.command: On each node confirm exactly one clock-sync service (chronyd, ntpd, or the cloud provider time source) is enabled and running (systemctl status chronyd, timedatectl, chronyc sources -v). All nodes must use compatible leap-smearing sources, and offsets must stay well within --max-offset (default 500ms).

remediation.command: Key requirements: - Run one clock sync service (NTP/chrony or provider's built-in time source) on each node. - Use compatible, leap-smearing time sources across all nodes. 1. Install and enable a time sync service (per environment): - AWS EC2: Configure each instance to use Amazon Time Sync Service via 169.254.169.123, verify via chronyc sources -v. - GCE: use GCE's internal NTP via metadata.google.internal;

title: Do Not Grant Sudo Privileges to the CockroachDB Process User
description: CockroachDB should run under a dedicated, non-root operating system account that has only the permissions required to read and write CockroachDB's data, log, and certificate directories. This dedicated service user (commonly cockroach) must not be granted sudo privileges or be included in any privileged system groups (such as wheel, sudo, or adm). The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when every cockroach start process runs as a non-root user that is not in the sudo, wheel, admin or root groups. Also review /etc/sudoers and /etc/sudoers.d for entries naming the cockroach user.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.3 Do Not Grant Sudo Privileges to the CockroachDB Process User

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo user=,args= | grep '[c]ockroach start') || exit 1; bad=0; for u in $(printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk '{print $1}' | sort -u); do [ "$u" = root ] && bad=1; if id -nG "$u" 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -qxE 'sudo|wheel|admin|root'; then bad=1; fi; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo privileged

remediation.command: Run CockroachDB as a dedicated non-privileged 'cockroach' user (User=cockroach in the unit), remove it from sudo/wheel groups (gpasswd -d cockroach wheel) and delete any sudoers entries for it.

title: Ensure Database Servers Are Isolated in a Separate Subnet with Restricted Ingress and Egress
description: The core requirement is to deploy CockroachDB nodes on private, non-public networks (subnets, VLANs, or VPC private segments) and to use strict firewall or security group rules to control access to the required ports. This ensures the database is shielded from the public internet and enforces least-privilege access.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.4 Ensure Database Servers Are Isolated in a Separate Subnet with Restricted Ingress and Egress

audit.command: Run cockroach node status --format=table and confirm node addresses are private (RFC 1918). Review host firewalls / security groups: 26257 (SQL/RPC) only from other nodes, approved app subnets and jump hosts; 8080 (DB Console) only from admin networks; no 0.0.0.0/0 ingress; egress limited to required destinations (NTP, KMS, backup storage).

remediation.command: 1. Place CockroachDB Nodes in Private Networks: Ensure all CockroachDB VMs are located in a private VLAN or non-internet-routable subnet. If a public IP is assigned for management, ensure it is not the primary address used for cluster communication and that its inbound ports are fully locked down. 2.

title: Ensure CockroachDB Logging Is Enabled and Logs Are Securely Stored
description: CockroachDB's built-in logging must remain enabled to capture database events, and log files should be stored in a secure location with appropriate access restrictions. Misconfiguration (for example an empty or invalid --log-dir) can prevent logs from being retained.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.1 Ensure CockroachDB Logging Is Enabled and Logs Are Securely Stored

audit.command: Run systemctl cat cockroach.service | grep ExecStart: it should set --log-dir=<path>, --log-config-file or --log={yaml} (otherwise logs go to <store>/logs). In that directory confirm cockroach.log, cockroach-security.log, cockroach-sql-audit.log and cockroach-sql-auth.log exist with recent timestamps, the directory is owned by cockroach with mode 700 or stricter, and log files are 640 or stricter.

remediation.command: mkdir -p /var/lib/cockroach/logs; chown -R cockroach:cockroach /var/lib/cockroach/logs; chmod 700 /var/lib/cockroach/logs; add --log-dir=/var/lib/cockroach/logs (or --log-config-file=<yaml>) to ExecStart in cockroach.service, then systemctl daemon-reload and perform a rolling restart.

title: Ensure Connection Authentication Logging Is Enabled
description: CockroachDB can log client connection attempts, successful logins, authentication failures, and session disconnections through the SESSIONS logging channel. By default, this channel's logging is disabled to minimize overhead on all clusters. Runs cockroach sql with --certs-dir ${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs} (a root or admin client certificate must be in it); the target node comes from COCKROACH_HOST (default localhost:26257) or COCKROACH_URL. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when server.auth_log.sql_connections.enabled and server.auth_log.sql_sessions.enabled are both true.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.3 Ensure Connection Authentication Logging Is Enabled

audit.command: out=$(cockroach sql --certs-dir="${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs}" --format=csv --execute "SHOW CLUSTER SETTING server.auth_log.sql_connections.enabled; SHOW CLUSTER SETTING server.auth_log.sql_sessions.enabled;" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -cx true || true

remediation.guidance: SET CLUSTER SETTING server.auth_log.sql_connections.enabled = true; SET CLUSTER SETTING server.auth_log.sql_sessions.enabled = true; and keep the SESSIONS channel routed to cockroach-sql-auth.log.

title: Restrict Access Using Host-Based Authentication
description: CockroachDB uses a host-based authentication (HBA) configuration to control which SQL connection attempts are allowed to proceed and which authentication methods they may use, based on the originating IP address and the SQL user. HBA rules are expressed in a PostgreSQL-compatible DSL and stored in the server.host_based_authentication.configuration cluster setting;
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.1 Restrict Access Using Host-Based Authentication

audit.command: Run SHOW CLUSTER SETTING server.host_based_authentication.configuration; Rules must list only approved IP addresses/CIDRs for each user and end with a rule that rejects everything else (e.g. host all all all reject). An empty value (the default, equivalent to host all all all cert-password) or broad 0.0.0.0/0 rules is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Define explicit whitelisted origins Construct an HBA configuration that lists only authorized IP ranges or hosts. For example: SET CLUSTER SETTING server.host_based_authentication.configuration = ' TYPE DATABASE USER ADDRESS METHOD host all jump_user 203.0.113.10/32 password host all app_user 198.51.100.0/24 password host all all all reject ';

title: Restrict and Secure Password Authentication
description: CockroachDB self-hosted clusters support several authentication methods for SQL clients, including passwords, SCRAM-SHA-256, TLS client certificates, and others such as GSSAPI/Kerberos (Enterprise), JWT, LDAP/AD and OIDC.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.2 Restrict and Secure Password Authentication

audit.command: Run SHOW CLUSTER SETTING server.user_login.password_encryption; (must be scram-sha-256) and review SHOW USERS; plus SELECT username FROM system.users WHERE "hashedPassword" IS NOT NULL. Privileged and service accounts should use certificates; any remaining password hashes should be SCRAM-SHA-256 and passwords must meet length policy (server.user_login.min_password_length).

remediation.command: 1. Enable SCRAM-SHA-256 for new passwords Configure the cluster to use SCRAM-SHA-256 for all newly set passwords: SET CLUSTER SETTING server.user_login.password_encryption = 'scram-sha-256'; This ensures that any CREATE USER ... WITH PASSWORD or ALTER USER ... WITH PASSWORD operations store SCRAM-SHA-256 hashes. 2.

title: Ensure Backups Are Encrypted Using an External Method
description: In self-hosted CockroachDB deployments, the Encryption-at-Rest (EAR) feature encrypts only the node's local on-disk data, including SSTables, write-ahead logs (WAL), and temporary files. EAR does not encrypt backup files created using the BACKUP statement.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.1 Ensure Backups Are Encrypted Using an External Method

audit.command: List recent backups with SHOW BACKUPS IN <collection URI> and SHOW BACKUP FROM <subdir> IN <URI>, and review scheduled backups (SHOW SCHEDULES). Each backup must be created WITH encryption_passphrase or kms = <KMS URI>, or written to storage with enforced server-side encryption; unencrypted backups are a finding.

remediation.command: Option 1 - Enable AES-256 Passphrase-Based Backup Encryption Configure backups to use passphrase-based encryption: BACKUP DATABASE <db> INTO 's3://bucket/path?AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=...&AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...' WITH encryption_passphrase = '<strong-passphrase>'; Use an external secret manager (e.g., Vault, AWS Secrets Manager) to store the passphrase (not documented in CockroachDB, but strongly recommended operationally).

title: Ensure Certificate File Permissions and Validity
description: While Control 1.3 ensures the cluster operates with TLS enabled, this control focuses on the security and maintenance of the certificate files residing on the node's file system. Critical security artifacts, specifically private keys (node.key, client.root.key), must be protected with strict OS-level file permissions to prevent unauthorized local users from reading the keys. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Checks ${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs}: every *.key must be 600/400 (no group/other access) and every *.crt must be unexpired. Also confirm the files are owned by the cockroach user and renew certificates nearing expiry.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.1 Ensure Certificate File Permissions and Validity

audit.command: d=${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs}; [ -d "$d" ] || exit 1; command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; bad=0; for k in "$d"/*.key; do [ -e "$k" ] || continue; p=$(stat -c %a "$k") || bad=1; [ $((0$p & 077)) -eq 0 ] || bad=1; done; for c in "$d"/*.crt; do [ -e "$c" ] || continue; openssl x509 -noout -checkend 0 -in "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 || bad=1; done; [ $bad -eq 0 ] && echo compliant || echo noncompliant

remediation.command: chmod 600 <certs>/*.key; chown -R cockroach:cockroach <certs>; regenerate expired or expiring certificates on the CA workstation (cockroach cert create-node / create-client) and reload them (SIGHUP or rolling restart).

title: Ensure remote connections via TCP/IP sockets are configured correctly
description: TCP/IP connections enable remote access to CockroachDB clusters across networks. CockroachDB supports multiple authentication methods for remote connections, with certificate-based authentication being the most secure option. All TCP/IP connections must use TLS encryption to protect data in transit. Remote connection security depends on proper network configuration, authentication method selection, and TLS settings.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.3 Ensure remote connections via TCP/IP sockets are configured correctly

audit.command: From a remote host run cockroach sql --insecure --host=<server>:26257 (must fail: server is not running in insecure mode) and cockroach sql --certs-dir=certs --host=<server>:26257 (must succeed). Check --listen-addr/--advertise-addr/--http-addr bind only intended interfaces and that clients use sslmode=verify-full.

remediation.command: Prerequisites: Complete certificate infrastructure setup as described in section 6.0. 1. Configure Server for Remote Access # Start CockroachDB listening on appropriate network interfaces cockroach start \ --certs-dir=certs \ --store=node1 \ --listen-addr=0.0.0.0:26257 \ --advertise-addr=database-server:26257 \ --http-addr=0.0.0.0:8080 \ --join=database-server:26257 # For multi-node clusters, configure each node cockroach start \ ...

title: Ensure Security Audit Logging Is Enabled
description: CockroachDB provides comprehensive audit logging capabilities to track security- relevant events including user authentication, privilege changes, and access to sensitive data. Role-based audit logging allows administrators to configure which users, roles, or statements should be logged, while sensitive access logging can track access to specific tables or databases containing sensitive information. Runs cockroach sql with --certs-dir ${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs} (a root or admin client certificate must be in it); the target node comes from COCKROACH_HOST (default localhost:26257) or COCKROACH_URL. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when sql.log.user_audit holds at least one audit rule; review that the rules cover privileged roles (admin, root) or ALL, and that the SENSITIVE_ACCESS channel is written to a protected sink.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.4 Ensure Security Audit Logging Is Enabled

audit.command: out=$(cockroach sql --certs-dir="${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs}" --format=csv --execute "SHOW CLUSTER SETTING sql.log.user_audit;" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'NR > 1 && /[^[:space:]"]/ {n++} END {print n ? "compliant" : "empty"}'

remediation.command: SET CLUSTER SETTING sql.log.user_audit = 'ALL ALL'; (or one 'admin ALL' / 'root ALL' line per privileged role), and route the SENSITIVE_ACCESS, USER_ADMIN and PRIVILEGES channels to protected log sinks.

title: Obtain the binary from an official and trusted source and verify the SHA-256 sum after downloading
description: CockroachDB server binaries and supporting tools must be obtained only from official Cockroach Labs release sources and verified using the published SHA-256 checksum before installation. The canonical sources for CockroachDB self-hosted binaries are: - The CockroachDB Releases pages, which link to official versioned binaries.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.1 Obtain the binary from an official and trusted source and verify the SHA-256 sum after downloading

audit.command: Review CI/CD pipelines, configuration-management code and install scripts: CockroachDB artifacts must be downloaded only from https://binaries.cockroachdb.com/ (or an internal mirror synced exclusively from it). For deployed versions, compare sha256sum of the downloaded archive with the published .sha256sum file; any other source or a checksum mismatch is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Reconfigure package pipelines Update all package managers, automation scripts, and manual runbooks to download CockroachDB binaries and tools only from: - https://binaries.cockroachdb.com/, or - A vetted internal mirror that pulls from this official source. 2. Download CockroachDB from official source and verify checksum #Example: Linux ARM64;

title: Ensure All Cluster Nodes Are Running the Exact Same Version, Including the Patch Release Number
description: All CockroachDB nodes in a self-hosted cluster must run the same major, minor, and patch version of the CockroachDB binary. The docs explicitly recommend that "all cluster nodes are running exactly the same CockroachDB version, including the patch release version number," and call out version mismatch as an essential alert condition.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.5 Ensure All Cluster Nodes Are Running the Exact Same Version, Including the Patch Release Number

audit.command: Run cockroach node status --certs-dir=<certs> --host=<node> --format=table (or the DB Console Node List) and compare the build/version of every node. All nodes must report the identical version, including the patch number; persistent version skew is a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Identify out-of-date nodes: cockroach node status --certs-dir=/var/lib/cockroach/certs --host=<node> -- format=table Review build or version fields to locate mismatched nodes. 2. Download the latest consistent binary Please refer to Control 1.1 3. Perform a rolling restart (Upgrade one node at a time.): - Use cockroach node drain with --shutdown to gracefully drain and then terminate the node's process.

title: Establish a Process for Rolling Upgrades to Apply Security Patches Without Downtime
description: CockroachDB supports rolling upgrades, allowing administrators to apply security patches, minor version updates, and configuration changes without cluster downtime. A rolling upgrade updates one node at a time, while the remaining nodes continue serving traffic and maintaining quorum.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.6 Establish a Process for Rolling Upgrades to Apply Security Patches Without Downtime

audit.command: Confirm a documented or automated rolling-upgrade procedure exists (one node at a time with cockroach node drain --shutdown, pre/post health checks, defined rollback plan, reference to Cockroach Labs upgrade docs). Run cockroach node status --all before upgrades: all nodes live, same version, no under-replicated ranges.

remediation.command: 1. Prepare for rolling upgrade: - Confirm cluster health and full replication: cockroach node status --certs-dir=/var/lib/cockroach/certs --host=<node> cockroach node status --certs-dir=/var/lib/cockroach/certs --all Backups are strongly recommended before upgrades. 2. Upgrade CockroachDB binary on each node (one at a time): - Use cockroach node drain with --shutdown to gracefully drain and then terminate the node's process.

title: Ensure Each CockroachDB Node Runs as a Dedicated Process on a Separate Host
description: For all self-hosted VM or bare-metal production deployments (on-premises or on cloud providers like AWS, GCP, Azure), each CockroachDB node must run as a single, dedicated cockroach start process on its own physical or virtual machine (VM). The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when exactly one cockroach start process runs on this host (FAIL when none runs). Also confirm the store directory is not shared with another node.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.2 Ensure Each CockroachDB Node Runs as a Dedicated Process on a Separate Host

audit.command: out=$(ps -eo args= | grep '[c]ockroach start') || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'END {print (NR == 1) ? "compliant" : NR " processes"}'

remediation.command: Stop the extra cockroach start processes (systemctl stop ...), provision a dedicated VM/host with its own storage for each additional node and redeploy it there.

title: Disable Linux Memory Swapping to Prevent Performance and Stability Issues
description: For production CockroachDB deployments on Linux VMs or bare-metal, it is a critical requirement to disable Linux memory swapping or ensure the system has adequate RAM to prevent swap usage. Swapping database memory pages to slow disk I/O introduces severe and unpredictable latency, compromising the database's performance and stability. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when /proc/swaps lists no active swap device. Also confirm at least 4 GiB RAM per vCPU and that --cache plus 2x --max-sql-memory stays below 80% of RAM.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.5 Disable Linux Memory Swapping to Prevent Performance and Stability Issues

audit.command: [ -r /proc/swaps ] || exit 1; awk 'NR > 1 {n++} END {print n+0}' /proc/swaps

remediation.command: swapoff -a, remove swap entries from /etc/fstab (and set vm.swappiness=0), and size RAM to at least 4 GiB per vCPU.

title: Set the File Descriptor Limit to at Least 15,000 to Accommodate Cluster Growth
description: CockroachDB can use a large number of open file descriptors, often more than is available by default. Therefore, note the following recommendations. For each CockroachDB node: - At a minimum, the file descriptors limit must be 1956 (1700 per store plus 256 for networking). If the limit is below this threshold, the node will not start. - It is recommended to set the file descriptors limit to unlimited; The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Reads the hard "Max open files" limit of the running cockroach process; it must be unlimited or at least 15000.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.7 Set the File Descriptor Limit to at Least 15,000 to Accommodate Cluster Growth

audit.command: pid=$(pgrep -o -x cockroach) || exit 1; awk '/^Max open files/ {print ($5 == "unlimited" || $5 + 0 >= 15000) ? "compliant" : "hard limit " $5}' /proc/$pid/limits

remediation.command: Set LimitNOFILE=35000 (at least 15000) in the [Service] section of cockroach.service (or a hard nofile limit in /etc/security/limits.conf for non-systemd setups), raise fs.file-max if needed, then restart the node.

title: Ensure Log Rotation and Retention Settings Are Configured
description: CockroachDB log rotation and retention must be configured to prevent uncontrolled growth and to preserve an appropriate history window. CockroachDB supports per-group rotation parameters that control both individual file size and total group retention. Each log file group can define: - max-file-size - maximum size of an individual log file before a new file is created.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.2 Ensure Log Rotation and Retention Settings Are Configured

audit.command: Run cockroach debug check-log-config (or grep -A10 file-groups: /etc/cockroach/logging.yaml) and confirm each production file group has suitable max-file-size and max-group-size (defaults 10MiB / 100MiB). Check that the on-disk log directory holds enough history to meet the retention policy and that logs are shipped off-node.

remediation.command: 1. Use defaults or define explicit rotation settings: If you do not configure a custom logging YAML, CockroachDB applies defaults of max- file-size: 10MiB and max-group-size: 100MiB to most file groups, which are acceptable for many small-to-medium deployments.

title: Ensure Database Monitoring and Alerting Are in Place
description: A robust monitoring and alerting system must be implemented for CockroachDB to continuously observe the health, performance, and security posture of the database cluster. CockroachDB exposes detailed metrics and events through its internal time- series database and provides a built-in Admin UI (DB Console) for visualization.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 3.4 Ensure Database Monitoring and Alerting Are in Place

audit.command: Confirm Prometheus (or equivalent) scrapes every node (grep cockroach /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml; curl -s http://<node>:8080/_status/vars | head), Grafana/DB Console dashboards show live data, and alert rules exist and are routed for node down >1 minute, disk capacity, clock offset, under-replicated ranges and certificate expiry.

remediation.command: 1. Integrate with Prometheus and Grafana: Configure Prometheus to scrape metrics from all CockroachDB nodes (default endpoint: http://<node>:8080/_status/vars). Example Prometheus job configuration: scrape_configs: - job_name: 'cockroachdb' scrape_interval: 10s static_configs: - targets: ['node1:8080', 'node2:8080', 'node3:8080'] Import the official CockroachDB Grafana dashboard JSON from Cockroach Labs to visualize performance data. 2.

title: Centralize and Standardize User Management
description: Self-hosted CockroachDB clusters should maintain consistent and centralized management of database user identities to ensure secure, controlled, and predictable access. CockroachDB supports several external authentication systems-such as OIDC, GSSAPI/Kerberos, and LDAP-but organizations may also centralize identity management by standardizing how CockroachDB accounts are created, assigned roles, and deprovisioned.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 4.4 Centralize and Standardize User Management

audit.command: Confirm a documented user lifecycle (approval, standard role assignment, prompt deprovisioning). Run SHOW USERS; and compare against the authorised user list/HR records: no orphaned, shared or unused accounts may remain. Where supported, check that LDAP/OIDC/Kerberos integration is used for human users.

remediation.command: 1. Establish a centralized user management process Document and enforce: - Account creation approval - Standardized role/privilege assignment - Required justification for role elevation - Timely account deprovisioning 2. Remove orphaned or unauthorized accounts DROP USER <username>; Only after confirming the user is no longer required and privileges are reassigned as needed.

title: Periodically Test Backup Recovery Procedures
description: Self-hosted CockroachDB deployments must regularly test backup recovery procedures to ensure that backups can be successfully restored, data integrity is preserved, and security controls remain effective during restoration. CockroachDB provides multiple backup and restore features, including full and incremental backups, encrypted backups, and backup validation tools.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.2 Periodically Test Backup Recovery Procedures

audit.command: Confirm documented restore procedures exist (backup locations, RESTORE of cluster/database/table into a non-production recovery cluster, decryption with the passphrase/KMS key). Review restore-test records: tests must run on a regular schedule and after changes to backup configuration, encryption, KMS keys, IAM or major upgrades, with data validation and measured RTO/RPO.

remediation.command: 1. Define a restore testing schedule Establish a policy requiring restore or backup validation testing at a regular cadence and after key changes, such as: - Changes to backup configuration or destinations. - Changes to backup encryption (for example, enabling encrypted backups or changing KMS configuration). - KMS key rotation or changes to encryption keys. - IAM or credential changes affecting access to backup storage or KMS.

title: Control Key Data Usage for Multi-Region Clusters with Data Localization Restrictions
description: In self-hosted CockroachDB multi-region clusters, organizations must ensure that Personally Identifiable Information (PII) or other regulated data is not used as part of primary key constraints or secondary indexes. In CockroachDB, primary keys define the primary index, and primary key columns are implicitly included in all secondary indexes. When a column is included in a primary key or index, its values are: 1.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 5.3 Control Key Data Usage for Multi-Region Clusters with Data Localization Restrictions

audit.command: If the cluster uses multi-region features (SHOW REGIONS FROM DATABASE; REGIONAL BY ROW / GLOBAL tables), identify tables holding PII subject to data-localization rules and review SHOW CREATE TABLE for each: PII must not be used in primary keys or secondary index keys (key data is replicated to meta ranges in all regions). Single-region clusters are not applicable.

remediation.command: 1. Replace PII-based keys with surrogate keys Refactor schemas so that primary keys use surrogate identifiers instead of PII. CockroachDB recommends: - Using UUID-typed columns with default values generated by gen_random_uuid() for single-column primary keys. - Using composite primary keys where the leading column is a well-distributed, non-sensitive identifier. Ensure PII columns are stored as regular, non-indexed fields where possible.

title: Ensure local connections via UNIX domain sockets are configured correctly
description: UNIX domain sockets provide secure local inter-process communication for database connections on the same host. When combined with certificate-based authentication (see section 6.0), UNIX domain sockets offer the most secure mechanism for local database access.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.2 Ensure local connections via UNIX domain sockets are configured correctly

audit.command: Check the --socket-dir used by cockroach start (default $TMPDIR); the socket (.s.PGSQL.26257) directory should be owned by cockroach and not world-writable (e.g. /var/run/cockroach, 755). Confirm cockroach sql --certs-dir=certs --host=<socket dir> --user=root works only with valid client certificates and that unauthenticated local logins fail.

remediation.command: Prerequisites: Complete certificate infrastructure setup as described in section 6.0. 1. Configure UNIX Domain Socket Location # Start CockroachDB with custom socket directory cockroach start \ --certs-dir=certs \ --store=node1 \ --listen-addr=localhost:26257 \ --socket-dir=/var/run/cockroach \ --http-addr=localhost:8080 # Ensure socket directory has appropriate permissions mkdir -p /var/run/cockroach chown cockroach:cockroach /var/run/cockroach ...

title: Ensure OCSP Certificate Revocation Checking Is Enabled
description: Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP) is a mechanism for checking whether a certificate has been revoked by its Certificate Authority (CA) before it expires. CockroachDB supports OCSP checking through the security.ocsp.mode cluster setting, which can be configured to verify certificate revocation status when validating client and node certificates. Runs cockroach sql with --certs-dir ${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs} (a root or admin client certificate must be in it); the target node comes from COCKROACH_HOST (default localhost:26257) or COCKROACH_URL. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when security.ocsp.mode is strict or lax (default off); strict is recommended where the OCSP responder is reliable.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.5 Ensure OCSP Certificate Revocation Checking Is Enabled

audit.command: out=$(cockroach sql --certs-dir="${COCKROACH_CERTS_DIR:-/var/lib/cockroach/certs}" --format=csv --execute "SHOW CLUSTER SETTING security.ocsp.mode;" 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk 'NR == 2 {v = tolower($0)} END {print (v == "strict" || v == "lax") ? "compliant" : "mode " v}'

remediation.guidance: SET CLUSTER SETTING security.ocsp.mode = 'strict'; (or 'lax' if OCSP availability cannot be guaranteed) and tune security.ocsp.timeout.

title: Ensure SQL Session Idle Timeouts Are Configured for SQL Roles
description: CockroachDB allows administrators to define role-level SQL session idle timeouts using the idle_in_session_timeout session variable. This setting ensures that any session authenticated under a given SQL role is automatically terminated after a defined period of inactivity. Configuring idle session timeouts for SQL roles provides a more granular control model than cluster-wide settings.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 6.6 Ensure SQL Session Idle Timeouts Are Configured for SQL Roles

audit.command: For every SQL role run SHOW DEFAULT SESSION VARIABLES FOR ROLE <role_name>; idle_in_session_timeout must appear with a non-zero value aligned with policy (e.g. 10m-30m for administrative roles, up to 1h for application roles with documented justification). Roles without it are a finding.

remediation.command: 1. Set idle timeout for a SQL role: Set a reasonable timeout for idle connections: ALTER ROLE <role_name> SET idle_in_session_timeout = '<duration>'; -- Example - set 30-minute idle timeout for a read-only role: ALTER ROLE table_reader SET idle_in_session_timeout = '30m';

title: Ensure CockroachDB systemd Service Files Are Enabled
description: Confirm, and correct if necessary, that the CockroachDB systemd service is enabled on Linux-based systems. This ensures CockroachDB starts automatically at system boot, recovers gracefully from crashes, and is consistently managed under a dedicated non-root service account.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 1.2 Ensure CockroachDB systemd Service Files Are Enabled

audit.command: Run systemctl list-unit-files | grep cockroach, then systemctl is-enabled cockroach.service and systemctl status cockroach.service, and ps -u cockroach -f | grep cockroach. A CockroachDB unit must exist, be enabled at boot, be active, and run as the dedicated cockroach user.

remediation.command: For each initial node of your cluster, complete the following steps: 1. Create the Cockroach directory: mkdir /var/lib/cockroach 2. Create a Unix user named cockroach: useradd cockroach 3. Move the certs directory to the cockroach directory: mv certs /var/lib/cockroach/ 4. Change the ownership of the cockroach directory to the user cockroach: chown -R cockroach /var/lib/cockroach 5.

title: Configure Transparent Huge Pages (THP) to madvise to Avoid Increased Memory Usage
description: Linux Transparent Huge Pages (THP) is a kernel feature that automatically manages large memory pages to improve performance for some workloads. However, for databases such as CockroachDB, this behavior can cause unpredictable latency spikes, increased memory fragmentation, and excessive CPU overhead due to THP defragmentation. Cockroach Labs recommends configuring THP to madvise instead of the default always mode. The benchmark rates this recommendation Manual; the automated check covers its objective pass criterion. Passes when madvise is the selected (bracketed) Transparent Huge Pages mode.
reference: CIS CockroachDB v25.x Benchmark v1.0.0 - 2.6 Configure Transparent Huge Pages (THP) to madvise to Avoid Increased Memory Usage

audit.command: out=$(cat /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled 2>/dev/null) || exit 1; printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -o '\[[a-z]*\]'

remediation.command: echo madvise > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled (and defrag), then persist it at boot (kernel parameter transparent_hugepage=madvise or a systemd unit).
